Those whose sins are washed away by meditation upon You become fortunate; they possess invincible prosperity, bodies full of joy, and are scorched by the intensity of their thirst [for worldly things]; they enjoy supreme excellence, have anger destroyed in an instant, and their lives are filled with auspiciousness; they possess surging power and blazing luster, have cast off formidable time, laugh within their hearts, and attain the secret of happiness.

His mind, which had spent its time in the leisurely enjoyment of tasting the flowing nectar of praise for the crest-jewel fashioned by the one whose banner is the young deer [Śiva], how could it find delight in another poet’s work—any more than a bee, preoccupied with the festival of drinking the filaments of a lotus, would find pleasure in another flower? (13) **Anvaya:** *yanmanaḥ niḥspada-mandaṃ bālakuraṅgaketanakṛtottaṃsapraśaṃsāmṛtasyandāsvādavinodanaiḥ kālam anayat...* **Translation:** His mind, which had passed its time slowly and motionlessly in the diversion of tasting the flow of nectar from the praises of the crest-jewel worn by the one whose emblem is the young deer... [how could it find delight elsewhere? (13)
How could there be any delight for that bee, who is intent on the festival of drinking the filaments of the lotus, in another flower, or likewise in any other poetic style? He who,
as an ornament upon his skull-topped staff, his crown, his hand, and his ears, bears the multitude of heads of the gods led by Brahmā and Upendra.

O Lord, the fortunate one whose mind is permeated by devotion to Your lotus feet certainly attains the renown of being the crest-jewel of those who possess the preeminent status in the three worlds. 14.

He who is the Lord generally bears upon his couch-frame, his crown, his hand, and his ears the garland of the heads of the gods led by Brahmā and Upendra as ornaments— he whose mind is permeated by devotion to the lotus-feet of that Lord, the fortunate one, certainly attains the renown of being the crest-jewel of those who enjoy preeminence throughout the three worlds.

Victorious is the ritual of worship of Śrīkaṇṭha: a mighty axe for the growing tree of delusion; an irresistible physician who cures the fever of passion; the limit that brings an end to the fierce curses of painful afflictions and the flood of poisons; the rising of the sun for the pair of cakravāka birds that are languishing eyes; and a flood of moonlight for the *cakkavāka* bird of the mind. (15)

Victorious is the ritual of worship of Śrīkaṇṭha—[a ritual] which is a great axe for the tree of delusion growing through successive births; a physician who brings relief by burning away the fever of passion that is otherwise difficult to ward off; the end of the fierce curse of afflictions as treacherous as a flood of poison; the rising of the sun for the pair of cakravāka birds that are languishing eyes; and a flood of moonlight for the cakora bird that is the mind. Thus it is.

Beholding the image of the one who bears the crescent moon as his crest-jewel—an image of wondrous and beautiful craftsmanship—the wonder of devotion repeatedly arises in the hearts of those of refined intellect.
Upon that image, the eyes of the long-lashed women fall again and again—eyes moist with the nectar of love, longing, alert, averted, smiling, and full of intent meaning. || 16 ||
Beholding the image of him whose crest-jewel is the moon of his lineage—an image of wondrous and beautiful arrangement—the wonder of devotion repeatedly manifests in the hearts of the wise.
Upon that [image], the glances of the long-lashed women fall: full of longing, tremulous, averted, smiling, full of intent, and moist with the nectar of love.
O Lord, those touched by devotion— having fastened a garland of flowers upon your body which has reduced the God of Love to ashes with the cords of their glances—

dispel the pain of love’s fever; their moon-like faces are distressed by the swaying of the swing, and their half-closed eyes find bliss in the flow of sandalwood paste from the creeper-like arms of their companions.

Anvaya: O Lord! Having bound a garland of flowers (*saumanasa*) upon Your body—which has reduced the God of Love to ashes with the nooses of Your glances—and which is touched by devotion, those women with moon-like faces, overwhelmed by the swaying of the swing, close their half-eyes in bliss from the flow of sandalwood paste from their creeper-like arms; thus, they shatter the painful torment of love.

O Lord, those fawn-eyed women whose pride has melted away from the god of love bathe Your feet with streams of water-drops trickling from the edges of their beautiful eyelashes— those very feet which, at the conclusion of worship, one repeatedly sprinkles with devotion while bowing low with abundant showers of tears born of intense joy.

Anvaya: O Lord! those fawn-eyed women, whose pride has melted away by passion, bathe Your two lotus feet with streams of teardrops flowing from the edges of their graceful eyelashes—tears shed repeatedly by them who, at the conclusion of Your worship, bow with devotion and drench the pair of Your lotus feet with abundant showers of tears of intense joy.

O Bhava, because he was unable to attack you directly due to your inexhaustible majesty and the intensity of the rows of fire-pikes on your forehead, the God of Love has surely abandoned you in person;
instead, he incessantly strikes those who are solely devoted to your service with the showers of arrows that are the side-glances of fawn-eyed women flickering near their ears. 19.
O Bhava! Because he is unable to attack you directly due to the intensity of the rows of fire-pikes on your forehead,

Smara— having disregarded you whose power of inauspicious influence is insupportable— surely strikes incessantly with the series of arrow-like sidelong glances flickering near the ears of fawn-eyed women, who are solely devoted to serving you.

Having been gradually led toward you through acquaintance with her companion, Devotion, she ascended the treacherous paths of the God of Love and wandered for a long time until she reached exhaustion.
Now, employing as her messenger the Goddess Sarasvatī, whose speech is ever-new and faultless, this Mind— possessed of intense passion— desires to approach you as her husband.

Having been gradually led toward openness through familiarity with her companion Devotion since childhood (by reason of the refinement of learning), she then ascended the paths of the God of the Five Arrows and wandered for a long time; now, having become a vessel of exhaustion (weariness), this mind of mine, its passion unrestrained,
desires to approach you as my husband, making the Goddess Bhāratī— whose speech is ever-new and faultless— my messenger.

Who else, other than you who are praised by the Lord of the Immortals, would have taken into his hand the poison— whose body is deep and voracious with billowing smoke, which mocks the splendor of the sun, which mangles the radiant beauty of the white-bodied Śrīkaṇṭha with its crackling hiss, and which emits sparks of fire from its towering form as it swallows?

Anvaya: O Blessed One! Apart from you, what other person, praised by the lords of the immortals, has seized in his hand the poison—which has a body as deep and voracious as a column of rising smoke, which mocks the brilliance of the sun, which muddies the white splendor of the body of the goddess Śrī with its flashing hisses, and from whose formidable form fiery sparks are falling—in order to swallow it?
With his neck embraced by serpents swinging from the mouths of baskets held in the hands of the servants of Yama, who are frantic with rage; uttering piteous cries of lamentation;

casting his eyes in all directions and intermediate points with his fortitude shattered; and seeking some protector capable of saving him—afflicted as he is, whom else but You would he choose for refuge at the moment of death? (22)

O All-pervading Lord! With his neck embraced by serpents swinging from the hollow of the hands of the servants of Yama, who are frantic with rage; uttering piteous cries of lamentation and casting his eyes in all directions and intermediate points; seeking one capable of protection, his fortitude shattered and tormented by death—whom other than You does he choose as his refuge?

O Lord, may the moonlight of your speech— white as kasha grass, illuminating the quarters with the rays of its ten teeth, raining down nectar capable of removing the harsh burning that nourishes the faults of worldly existence, and drawing away the uneven darkness of a world whose light has been crushed— take its place upon your head like the crescent moon.

O Lord! May your speech—the words of fearlessness—which, like the digit of the moon upon your head, showers nectar with its pure rays capable of removing the harsh burning that nourishes worldly defects; which draws away the intense darkness of the world for those oppressed by it; and which bestows the radiance of *kāśa* grass upon the ten directions—may that speech establish its place upon your face.

O Lord, since Your heart—which is preeminent in the sweetness blossoming from the full ripening of compassion—remains expansive and indifferent toward me in this calamity of the terrible afflictions of saṃsāra;
O Master, it is my own cruel fate that causes this person, exhausted by the long journey, to depart fruitlessly from the shore of the ocean of jewels due to his own wicked deeds.

*Anvaya:* O Lord! Since Your heart, which is the foremost in the sweetness blossoming from the full ripening of compassion, [is indifferent] in this calamity of the terrible afflictions of *saṃsāra*... [toward me].
She treats me with disdainful indifference; this is my own cruel fate. For a person exhausted by a long journey departs fruitlessly from the shore of a treasure of jewels due to his own misdeeds.

Such is this body of mine, which has become the object of the sidelong glances of young Mālava women whose fingers are busily occupied with waving chowries that sway playfully like dense waves in the ocean of her beauty.

The fortunate ones bear two feet that are kissed by the crowns of their rival vassals, who are agitated by the prospect of serving them and coming into their presence; these feet are the very abode of good fortune and prosperity.

Those who are skilled in discerning the lineage possess a body that is the abode of the fortune of good luck— a body whose two feet are licked by the crowns of their vassals as they bow in agitation to announce their presence for service, and which has become the object of the side-long glances of young Mālava women whose fingers are busily occupied with chowries swaying playfully like thick waves in the ocean of beauty.

And where, at the foot of trees upon soft, unfolding meadows on the banks of the celestial river, those who fear the intense leaping of the noose-mouthed serpents— those kings whose forms were terrifying with the knitting of brows formed by swelling,
short pride— now dwell, subsisting on roots and fruits, seeking the taste of the nectar of tranquility. (26)
And furthermore, [there were] those virtuous ones who,

seeking the taste of the nectar of tranquility and fearing the intense leaping over the nooses of kings— whose faces were terrifying with frowns formed by towering, swaying pride— dwelt at the foot of trees on the banks of the celestial river amidst soft, burgeoning meadows, subsisting on roots and fruits.

And herein we dwell happily, amidst this grand display, where the results of our undertakings are pure and their sole noble task is to soothe the distress of people prostrated by the calamities of ill-fortune— results that are comparable to tiny droplets of frost trembling upon the edges of lotus petals swaying in the gentle, ripening breeze. (27)

And furthermore, while this worldly display is like a mere fragment of frost trembling on the edges of lotus petals shaken by the movement of a gentle, changing breeze, those virtuous ones— who possess the undertaking of pure deeds whose sole purpose is the act of quenching the suffering of people exhausted by the calamities of an evil age—
live happily and without fear. Having attained this human state, which is beheld by the side-glances of Fortune blooming upon their stainless limbs, they rejoice eternally with herds of elephants.
And having attained a stainless human birth,
gazed upon by the side-long glances of Lakṣmī sporting on their laps, they remain eternally joyful and rejoice without fear amidst herds of elephants;
and with their bodies covered in horripilation arising from hearing the nectar of the songs sung by the celestial damsels of Indra, they dwell in the midst of heaven.
They dwell before Him in the midst of His own light.
This is the supreme grace of the Lord of the entire universe, the sole protector of the helpless, the ocean of the nectar of compassion, the husband of Girijā.
What lover of contemplation would not seek to attain Him through hymns of praise offered with mature devotion, in order to obtain the pure fruit of deeds that bestow happiness?

He rejoices with unrestrained devotion. (A Kulaka of five verses) The grammatical connection (*anvaya*) is as follows: This [attainment] is the supreme grace of the Lord of the entire universe, who is solely intent on protecting those without refuge, the ocean of the nectar of compassion, the husband of Girijā. [One should worship] that [grace], which is the pure fruit of deeds that bestow happiness, with feelings of love offered by the mature [devotees]. (29)
Who that delights in discernment and possesses unwearied devotion would not rejoice in attaining [Thee] through hymns of praise?

O Lord, Thy speech is a rain of nectar, distilling the most sweet of essences; Thy two hands are purified by friendship with the rows of dust from the friction of Thy footstool; and Thy mind is the abode of rest for the garden of compassion, matured by its own spontaneous activity.
O Great One, this is the ripening for those who have approached you, the ocean of the nectar of unmitigated grace.

Anvaya: O Lord! Your vision is a rain of nectar; your speech flows with the most sweet of essences; your hands are purified by friendship with the rows of dust from the friction against the footstool of your own feet; your mind is the resting place for the garden of compassion ripened through your independent conduct—oh! such is the fruition for those who have resorted to you, an ocean of the nectar of unceasing grace.

The kings instantly delight his single footstool with their heads, which are adorned by the spreading radiance of the brilliant jewels in their crowns and joined together in hollowed palms. And he alone, the fortunate one, bears that splendor characterized by a white umbrella as bright as moonlight,
a beautiful white upper garment, and the noble pearl necklaces swaying from the lotus-hands of the exuberant Goddess Rāmā.

The lords of sages praise his wonderful life-story with words that distill nectar into the hollows of their ears; the excellent women of the Vidyādharas sing it in songs. News of the generosity and courtesy of this virtuous man spreads through assemblies of the learned, and his fame awakens within the auspicious compositions of the finest poets.

Or what else? He beholds nothing other than the terrifying mouth of Time, distorted by a frown, with teeth formidable as they flash like sparks from tongues of fire tawny as flames—enough of this! O Master, in the forest edge, lovely with the dance of graceful creepers swaying in the gentle breeze, let him who is free from the envy of worldly peace worship you—the physician for the world paralyzed by ignorance. (The Tilaka)

The lineages of kings clearly color the footstool of that one blessed man with their heads— joined in hollowed palms and radiant with the expansive splendor of the jewels in their crowns; and that one blessed man alone bears the Goddess of Fortune, who is adorned with a white umbrella bright as moonlight, auspicious white upper garments,
and magnificent pearl necklaces swaying from the lotus-hands of the goddess Rāmā, while the lords of sages [glorify her] with words that distill nectar into the hollows of their ears.

The excellent women of the Vidyādharas praise his wondrous life with their words and sing of it in songs. In assemblies of the learned, the report of this virtuous man’s generosity and courtesy spreads; amidst the auspicious compositions of eminent poets, his fame remains awake. What more need be said? He is capable of [consuming] that which is terrifying, with brows knitted in a frown, and formidable with teeth flashing like sparks from tongues as tawny as the flames of fire.

He does not see the mouth of Death. O Lord! He who, free from envy, should worship you—the physician for the world stupefied by ignorance—in the forest retreat beautiful with the dancing of lovely creepers swayed by gentle breezes;
[Death], drawing his bow back to his ear, strikes him silently with a multitude of arrows consisting of the sidelong glances of women's eyes, inflicting harm without cause.

The flower-bowed god [Kāma], the black serpent with a gaping mouth, his wide blade flashing like a hiss, his matted locks thick with the flickering flames of potent poison—desiring to devour our bodies, he is terrifying; where shall we go? (34)

Therefore, for us who are afflicted by the suffering and calamity arising from the ripening of our sudden and fluctuating good and evil karmas, you alone are the refuge—you who are an ocean of incessant compassion, a kinsman to the distressed; whose footstool is licked by the flames of the rows of rubies in the crowns of the hosts of gods bowing in devotion and faith; and whose nature is to protect those without protection. (35) [A yugma]

The flower-bowed god of love, acting without cause or provocation, draws his bow back to his ear and silently strikes us with volleys of arrows consisting of the sidelong glances from the corners of women's eyes. A terrifying black serpent, its hood wide with hissing and its head thick with flickering tongues of fierce, spreading venom, desires to kill us and swallows our very bodies; where can we go? Therefore, O Lord!

For us, who are afflicted by the suffering and calamities resulting from the ripening of our various good and evil deeds that arise without cause, you alone are the refuge— you who are an ocean of incessant compassion, a kinsman to those in distress,

whose footstool is licked by the flames of the rows of rubies upon the crowns of the hosts of gods prostrating with continuous streams of devotion and faith, and whose nature is to protect the helpless. You alone are the refuge.

O Earth, the mother of all beings, whose birth as the source of all medicinal herbs was never again repeated anywhere, where there is no contact with the calamities that cause even the steadfast to fall; you who have made your abode manifest upon the couch of the serpent Śeṣa,
and who constantly make the virtuous man a vessel for prosperity— homage, homage to you, the very commencement of the removal of sin!

This Earth, whose birthplace is the serpent Śeṣa—the source from which all medicinal herbs arise without exception, where even a touch of trembling never occurred, and where she stands above those subject to downfall—constantly makes people worthy vessels of prosperity; [O] sinless one, at the very beginning of the creation of the primordial form, she was... [sinless].
Salutations be to You, whose majesty is like that of Maghavat (Indra), and who are the primary means [of liberation].

In this essence-less cycle of existence, virtuous action—primarily characterized by Dharma—is the supreme good; for the wise, Dharma, which bestows happiness, leads to perfection through the cause of purification. For those accomplished ones who have fixed their longing upon purity, nothing else remains.
O Blessed One, even that water which, without destroying calamities, nourishes the three worlds is Your own delusive power; salutations to You! 37.

In this utterly worthless cycle of existence, virtuous action centered on Dharma is what brings happiness; yet even Dharma here serves for the success of the wise who seek purity as a means to purification—for without it, there is no destruction of calamities for those accomplished ones who are intent upon purity. O Blessed One! Even that water which nourishes the three worlds is but a manifestation of Your power; salutations to You!

O Fire, you who alone, being ever-present and free from disease, sustain this world by releasing it from illness; you who are the cause of well-being for all creatures within it whose calamities are manifested by cold and fear; you who dispel the misfortunes of the gods with oblations and those of sacrificers with their abundant mental resolves—such is your majesty; salutations to you!

O All-pervading Lord! Apart from that Fire which, existing perpetually within living beings in the form of the digestive fire (*jaṭharāgni*), sustains this world by its health-giving nature, there is no other cause for the well-being of creatures whose calamities are manifested through the fear of cold. He who dispels the affliction of the gods—manifested as their lack of satisfaction—by means of abundant oblations, and who likewise dispels the affliction of sacrificers through his conceived intentions (*saṅkalpa*), he is that very one.

Salutations to You, whose power is Fire—the embodiment of sovereign majesty. Abiding within, You conceal the fivefold dissolution of the worlds; having established the five stable elements, You constantly expand wherever the wheel of light resides. It is in You that the abode of the three worlds maintains its stability, as You bear the form of the support for all beings.
The wind spreads its pervasive power; salutations to you! Salutations to you! || 39 ||

Anvaya: O Blessed One! That wind which, abiding within (the body) in five ways (through the five divisions of prāṇa, apāna, etc.), arrests the dissolution of the worlds into the five elements; wherein, having established a continuous state of stability, the wheel of light spreads forth;
and wherein the abode of the three worlds maintains its steadiness—this very wind, bearing a form that serves as the support of all beings, belongs to You.
Salutations to You, who manifest Your sovereign power—

that power by which the entire mass of the cosmic egg spreads out like a simple gourd or pumpkin, and even that water which displays its stability and resounding roar [is supported] within the structural joints of Your body; and even the wind, though vast, is able to sustain only a tiny fraction of those splendors which constitute the foundation of all light.
O you who exist as that very form, O sky, salutations to you! || 40 ||
O Bhava! That water—in which the cosmic egg, resembling a simple gourd or bottle-gourd, floats—is itself but a gurgling ripple;

that wind—which spreads stability within the structural joints of those waters—is itself unable to sustain even a tiny fraction of the vast expanse of space; and that space constitutes Your very body, the substratum of all luminous powers—to You, such as You are, [our salutations].
Homage!

He who brings about the fulfillment of these Vedas— which were born together with the four-faced [Brahmā] from his four mouths during the act of creating mankind, and which brought joy to those dwelling in heaven— by means of his merit-bestowing rites, is truly a sacrificer.
Your body does not undergo contact with calamity; homage to you, homage to you! || 41 ||

O Blessed One! To that performer of sacrifices whose body is Yours— He who, having brought delight to the celestial beings through the four mouths of the Creator who possesses such skill in the act of creating living beings, brings about the fulfillment of these Vedas of expansive luster by means of His constant, merit-bestowing rites, and who remains untouched by the touch of calamity— to Him, to You, let there be salutation.

O you who, with your swaying rays, enable the gods to sustain their lives through whiteness; you who, as the abode of intense bliss, manifest the breaking of the fast for the ancestors during the dark fortnight; you who, filling the vast firmament and quelling the darkness, nourish the full radiance of all medicinal herbs—O bodiless Moon, you are here; salutations to you!

That moon, whose body is vast, is your own immense form; for with its rays swaying in the bright fortnight (*dhavale*), it provides the sustenance of life, while in the dark fortnight (*bahule*), it becomes the abode of intense bliss for the ancestors and thus spreads their ritual feast (*pāraṇam*). Likewise, by making the great firmament free from darkness, it nourishes the full splendor of all medicinal herbs. This very moon is your own body.
Salutations to him!

To him whom the virtuous worship with joy at dawn upon this path that shatters [darkness], like a traveler, for the sake of bestowing light upon the world that was wearying in the wilderness of gloom; and whom the wise meditate upon in the evening as a state of concentration (*samādhi*) that dispels mental anguish, presiding over the rite of twilight (*saṃdhyā-vidhi*).
You are established here by excellence; you are that Sun-god, O possessor of true rays—salutations to you!

On this path that shatters [darkness], you are that Mihira (the Sun), whom the wise—established in perfect concentration (*samādhi*) and having overcome all mental afflictions (*ādhi*)—revere with excellence as they have arisen at dawn, joyful like a traveler in the midst of the darkness, for the sake of bestowing light upon the world; and whom they meditate upon at evening according to the twilight rite (*saṃdhyā-vidhi*). O you of auspicious rays! Salutations to you!

Salutations to You, that Supreme Brahman, whose glory cannot be measured by direction, place, form, or time; who is the great seed of the multitude of beings, from whom the entire collection of things within the three worlds evolves;
into whom the universe dissolves at the end—like a variety of ornaments into gold—and who remains undivided even when those [objects] are divided. Salutations to You!

O Bhava! You are that Supreme Brahman, whose glory cannot be measured by lineage, direction, form, or time; who is the great seed of the multitude of beings; and from whom the entire range of objects within the three worlds arises as either an illusory manifestation (*vivarta*) or a transformation (*pariṇāma*). Just as various ornaments are withdrawn back into gold, so too does the universe dissolve into you at the end. To you, who remain undivided even among divided living beings, I offer my salutation.
Thus, O Lord whose crest is the moon, may these hymns of mine—manifesting as pure pearls slipping from the oyster of my mouth which is opened by the swelling flood of Sarasvatī;

capable of pacifying the exhaustion of the hearts of sensitive souls tormented by the calamities of intense misfortune; and strung upon the firm thread of an intellect that rivals the tips of darbha grass—be [fruitful].
May they become ear-ornaments. || 45 ||

(1) The divine creation is of eight kinds, that of the animals is fivefold, and the human is of one kind; such, in brief, is the elemental creation. (Sāṃkhya Doctrine) [Anvaya: O peak of the moon! thus...

May these well-spoken verses of mine become ear-ornaments for you—verses which possess the clarity of pearls emerging from the oyster-like mouths opened by the swelling flood of Sarasvatī; which are capable of pacifying the exhaustion of the hearts of the sensitive who are fainting under the heat of intense calamities; and which are strung upon the firm thread of an intellect that rivals the tips of *darbha* grass.

Thus ends the thirty-third hymn, the *Karṇapūra-stotra*, in the *Stutikusumāñjali* dedicated to the Blessed Maheśvara, composed by the great Kashmiri poet Śrī Jagaddharabhaṭṭa, together with the commentary *Premamakaranda*.
[Now begins] the thirty-fourth hymn.

May Śarva— the face of the three-eyed one, whose eyelashes are like flickering tongues of fire from the blazing sun and moon within the expansion of his luster intent on removing the heavy fever of the surging pride of Kandarpa; who,
raining down gold that satiates the mind and allays the exhaustion of excessive thirst, bestows well-being and joy upon the sinless people— protect us from sin.
May it bring about inexhaustibility for you. || 1 ||

May Śarva, whose face is like that of the three-eyed god with its thick lashes flickering like flames of fire, the moon, and the newly risen sun— a manifestation of splendor intent on removing the heavy fever of the pride of Kāma as he advances—
may he, who joyfully creates a people free from sin, bestow upon you imperishable well-being through a golden rain that satisfies the mind and allays the exhaustion of excessive thirst.

Just as these words of yours are worthy of praise— serene, radiant with the composition of the vibration of incomparable aesthetic flavor (rasa), auspicious, bound with wit, and casting away all blemish— so may the excellent,
faultless crescent moon placed upon the matted locks of Bharga, that praiseworthy face which shatters the most powerful darkness, be the ornament for you. 2.

Anvaya: O Blessed One! Just as this auspicious, playful, and praiseworthy speech of Yours—which is free from blemish, gracious, and filled with the composition of the vibration of the nectar of the peerless Rasa—is worthy of adoration; even so, may the faultless crescent moon, the excellent ornament of Bharga, which rests upon His matted locks, which is praiseworthy, and which shatters the most intense darkness, destroy your misfortune.

May He—who resides in the six chakras; who is impetuous in the expansion of the six paths (adhvans); who is bold in the composition of creation; who is the Indra of the true wheel of Brahman, intent on the recitation of the ever-fresh, prostrate, and novel hymns; who assumes the role of the destroyer of Dakṣa’s sacrifice; who is praised for His aim of destroying the base and the pathless; who has destroyed the mud of worldly association; and who makes the multitude of attendants immovable—may He destroy all misfortune for you! 3.

Established within the six chakras of the lineage, impetuous in the expansion of the six paths, skilled in the composition of creation, the sovereign of the true wheel of the Supreme Brahman through the recitation of ever-fresh and prostrate hymns; bearing the nature of the destroyer of Dakṣa’s sacrifice, praised for the destruction of the lowest and the non-path; with the mire of worldly association destroyed, fashioning the multitude of Gaṇas as immovable—may that Bharga grant you peace.

Salutations to him who delights the Lord who slays Kaṃsa— He whose lotus-dwelling is the chest, whose hands bear the blazing conch and discus, who reclines upon a serpent-couch, who is borne by the best of birds, and who stands on one leg; and salutations to Him who, holding a banner that binds Dharma and a water-pot in His hand, proclaims the greatness of those established in their vows.
May He, the Imperishable, who is constantly remembered by those who bow down, destroy your sin. || 4 ||

He who eternally delights the bowing devotee— himself imperishable— who gladdens the Lord Viṣṇu (who has his abode on the chest, whose lotus-like hand-palms shine with the conch and discus, who slew Kaṃsa, who rests upon a serpent-couch, and whose vehicle is the best of birds), as he occupies half [of the Harihara form] (occupying the right half); and who likewise delights him as he stands in the vow, praising and remembering [the Lord], by assuming the form of Dharma standing upon a banner while holding a water-pot in his hand, thereby beautifying his body.
May misfortune befall you!

May the Ganges—with its dark, moving waves like the throats of intoxicated buffalo, and with its splashing waves that seem to reach for the heavens—rain down [blessings] upon him who protects his circle of devotees from the fear of Yama’s soldiers; who is worthy of the assembly, accessible to those nearby, who considers himself blessed, who is generous, who is overcome by affection, and who is established as the foremost of the council.
May Tryambaka, upon whose lap always rests the elephant-faced Ganesha, grant you prosperity.

May Tryambaka— the one whose throat is dark like a fresh *garava* buffalo, whose celestial Gaṅgā flows with waves dancing upon his crest, and who forever bears the elephant upon his lap— shower prosperity upon you as he protects the circle of his devotees from fear of Yama’s messengers; a group that is accompanied by its kin, easily accessible, self-conceited in its merit, generous, subservient to his affection, and established as the foremost in the assembly.
May the dust of the Lord’s feet— the water which makes the grass mat tremble, the serpent with thick venom clinging to His neck,

the sky, the wind, the harsh rays of the sun, the fire, the moon, and the garment— grant you freedom from sin. May the hide upon His shoulder, possessing the luster of gold, the mass of matted hair, the sandalwood paste applied to every limb, and the ash white as the petals of the *saptacchada* tree, likewise purify you.

Wearing his matted locks (*jaṭājūṭa*) which quiver in the water of the Gaṅgā; binding to his neck a serpent dripping with potent venom; attaining the state of the earth, the sky, the sun, the fire, the moon, and the atmosphere by binding them [to himself]; wearing upon his shoulder a shield as bright as the sun; binding his mass of hair into the form of sandalwood, white as the petals of the *saptacchada* tree; and applying ashes white as those petals to every limb—he is Aja.

May your impurity be cleansed by that which is immediately free from the seizing grip of pride, abandoned by attachment to worldly associations, established in pure being (*sattva*), and having attained reality; which, through the effort of its contact, dissolves this [world] while being itself stainless; and which, devoted to truth and what is wholesome, bestows purity.
May that mind of the one who bows at the pair of feet of Smara’s enemy [Śiva] bring you auspiciousness. || 7 ||

May that pure mind of one who bows at the feet of the Destroyer of Smara grant you peace— a mind which has immediately cast off the grasp of pride, whose darkness is destroyed, which has abandoned attachment and worldly involvement, which abides in goodness, which has realized the truth, whose bonds of all connections are loosening as they are washed away by impurities, which is capable of enduring the effort of contact [with the divine], which is compassionate and free from the ego, and which is devoted to what is real and wholesome.

It is true that the dense mass of sins of anyone who has fixed their faith upon the touch of his feet and whose mind is intent on clearly pacifying suffering, is inevitably destroyed; its impurity is made manifest. May the head of that Bull-bannered Lord, the refuge of the moon, which dispels all fear, which destroys trembling, and which possesses a luster delightful through contact with prosperity, cast away your misfortune.

For whom, whose mind is intent on pacifying manifest suffering and who has fixed their faith upon the touch of his feet, will the dense mass of sins—which is clearly visible—not certainly perish? (The implication is: for everyone indeed. May the head of that Abhayakara—the one who rides upon the bull—grant you peace; its radiance is delightful through contact with prosperity, and it has destroyed all trembling. It is a refuge for the moon.

May the Omniscient One—who manifests his utterly pure inner self as a refuge for the helpless, who incessantly shatters the deceit of the eyes, speech, and the paralysis of the limbs; who, being skilled in bringing rest to the multitude of beings, destroys the continuous chain of births and karmas; and who increases the supreme goal that has destroyed all impurities—may he increase your inexhaustible prosperity.

The Omniscient One (the Supreme Lord), who—manifesting an inner sense that is utterly pure, capable of providing refuge to the helpless, and standing right before us—constantly shatters the hypocrisy of eye-rolling, frowning, and facial paralysis; who is skillful in removing the exhaustion of the multitude of living beings; who thoroughly churns away (and thus exhausts) the cycle of births for transmigrating souls by destroying the continuity of karma; and who has destroyed all impurities—he [bestows] upon you the imperishable goal, the ultimate reality.
May he increase [our prosperity],

as he wanders at will through the dwellings of crystal and emerald, across the Malaya and Mandara mountains, within the Sahya range where Gandharvas and Yakṣas rejoice, along the golden ridges and amidst the Kalpa trees; passing through the auspicious abode of Indra, the laughing palace, the Nandana grove, and the theater of heaven.
May he who crushes the forces of the enemy gratify you every day. || 10 ||

May he who crushes the forces of his enemies, whose conduct is independent, and who— traversing the mountain Kailāsa, the abode of the moon-stone, then the Malaya and Mandara mountains where Gandharvas and Yakṣas rejoice within, and likewise the Sahya mountain which possesses golden ridges and is filled with the interior of wish-fulfilling trees; and further, traversing the auspicious palace of Indra, the abode of laughter, the celestial theater, and the Nandana grove— gratify you day by day.

May he who clearly beholds—without ever leaving the soles of his feet—the one seated upon a lotus, holding a lotus in hand, with the face of a noble elephant, known as Nandana and Skanda; Parjanya, the swan, the lotus, the thousand-eyed Indra, and Agni the consumer of oblations with his staff; the one resembling a Rakshasa, the first [element] situated in water, the wind, the one with mortal wings, and the destroyer of sacrifices—he shall sweep away your sin.
The sequence is as follows: he who is capable of not abandoning the soles of his feet [the connection "capable of not abandoning the soles of his feet" applies to each instance];
[Brahmā] seated upon a lotus; [Viṣṇu] with a lotus in his hand; [Gaṇeśa] whose face is like that of the best of elephants; [Kārttikeya] known by the name Skanda; [Parjanya] the son; [Sūrya] the swan;
[Candra] the lotus; [Indra] the thousand-eyed; [Yama] the consumer of oblations together with his staff; [Nirṛti] resembling a Rākṣasa; [Varuṇa] the first among those dwelling in the water.

May that Lord draw away your sin— he who, as the unborn one, manifests the entire unmanifest world-city, and he who, as the infinite one who subdues the pride of Smara, protects it; and may he, who perceives the Wind, the Mortal (Agni), Kubera, and the Sacrifice-slayer (Śiva), behold you with perfect vision.
May he who withdraws [the world] without succession— that three-eyed one, whose knowledge is unimpeded in the task of composing this treatise on the fruitfulness of tantras and mantras,
and who is supremely intent on revealing the path accessible to the virtuous— grant you non-duality.

He who, when the quality of *rajas* predominates, being the lotus-born (*abjaja*), manifests the entire world which was unmanifest; likewise, he who, through the predominance of *sattva*, being the infinite (*ananta*), protects the entire world; and similarly, he who, when *tamas* is predominant, being Smara-yama-damana (in the form of Rudra), withdraws the entire world simultaneously—such is he whose wisdom is vast in the task of composing this work on the successful application of *tantras* and *mantras*.

May Śaṅkara— the destroyer of worldly suffering, whose third eye is supreme in revealing the path accessible to the virtuous, who is the bestower of bliss through his excellent teaching of the true meaning, who is praised by those of foremost wisdom, and who is bowed to by the best of gods— touch you with the non-dual reality, which is that which is to be seen. May he, who is composed in verse, grant you this.

May that hymn of supreme syllables— pouring forth like rain that extinguishes the heat of worldly toil, consisting of the nectar of divine play, worthy of being heard through the discourse of one whose resolve is truth, auspicious, and bestowing wealth—
bring you a new and noble understanding. 13.
May that Śaṅkara, the best of gods, the destroyer of evil, whose lineage is renowned, grant you—[to be beheld with curiosity by those of refined taste]—this hymn of praise in excellent syllables:

which is composed in verse, supremely devoted to the correct exposition of meaning, bestowing bliss, praised by those of foremost wisdom; which destroys the affliction born of the threefold fever, rains down the waters of joy, is pleasant to hear as it speaks of truthful resolve, auspicious, bringing fortune, ever-new, and preeminent.

May this hymn, titled *Agryavarṇastava* (a compound formed by the elision of the middle term, meaning "the hymn of the foremost letter" or "the hymn composed by the one of foremost caste"), composed by the Kāśmīraka great poet Śrī Jagaddharabhaṭṭa—a twice-born of preeminent complexion—cause [you] to understand [the Lord].
(The sense is: may it, out of compassion, cause you to hear it yourself and awaken others as well.
Thus ends [this work] dedicated to the Blessed Maheśvara, accompanied by the *Premamakaranda*, composed by the illustrious Kāśmīraka great poet Śrī Jagaddharabhaṭṭa.
In the *Stutikusumāñjali*, the hymn of supreme praise (*agryavarṇastotra*) is completed. This is the thirty-fifth hymn:
He is the protector of the protectorless, the refuge for those without refuge, the guide for the afflicted, the shelter for the fearful, and the supporter of the weary.
Victorious in the three worlds is the Enemy of Death, who is a friend, a kinsman, a master, a refuge, a benefactor, an excellent teacher, a father, a mother, and a brother.

He is the protector of the orphaned, the refuge for those without recourse, the guide for the distressed, the shelter for the fearful, and the sustainer of the weak [the term *bharavaśaḥ* is a conventional epithet meaning "one who bears the burden"]. He is the bestower of fortitude, a friend [who provides consolation to those who disclose their own condition], a kinsman [who does not abandon one even in times of crisis], a master, a sanctuary, a benefactor, a supreme teacher [the instructor of his own teaching which is the cause for attaining liberation], and a father.
Victorious in the three worlds is the Enemy of Death, who is [as dear as] a mother and a brother!

When, having worshipped with love the Moon-Peaked Lord (Śiva), whose summit is adorned with noble Mandāra flowers—my body decorated with horripilation born of intense joy—shall I honor the All-pervading Lord with words of praise filled with the humming of wild bees exulting in their intoxication from the thick fragrance? 2.

When, with my body adorned by horripilation, shall I worship the Lord with words of praise—resonant with the humming of wild bees exulting in the fragrance of their clustered honey—having devoutly worshipped Mount Candraśikhara, whose peaks are fashioned from noble Mandāra trees?

From here [is] the suffering of dualities; from here [is] the state of the mirage of sense-objects; from here [is] the terror of old age, death, and disease; and from here [is] that which is easily attained by all.
How could a noble person, even one of firm resolve, allow his own well-being to be destroyed by terrible and great delusions that strike away the radiance of awakening? (3)

On this side are the afflictions of the pairs of opposites; on this side is the state of the mirage of sense objects; on this side is the terror of old age, death, and disease; on this side is everything easily obtained; and on this side, the radiance of awakening is struck down by terrible, great delusions. Thus, because the mind is agitated by many obstacles, how could even a noble person of firm resolve accomplish what is beneficial for his own self?

This host of obstacles, which acts as a rival to the drying up of the entire flood of afflictions and employs the method of bringing about powerful calamities, reveals itself; it suddenly obscures the eye called discernment (*viveka*) for the virtuous, by which means a vast fall occurs at every step into the abyss of worldly existence (*bhava*). (4)

This aforementioned multitude of obstacles, which acts as a hindrance to the drying up of the entire flood of afflictions, manifests a process that brings about powerful calamities; it obscures the eye known as discernment even for the wise, by which a massive fall occurs at every step into the abyss of worldly existence for embodied beings.

Then, having attained devotion to you— which is capable of bringing about his cessation [of suffering]— and having reached your gracious gaze of intense luster, those of noble intellect perceive you, whose nature is light and who are hailed as the Swan, with their own exceedingly pure vision, and thereby cast off the blinding darkness of delusion.

The syntactical connection (*anvaya*) is as follows: Then, O Blessed One! having attained devotion to you—which possesses dense luster and extends the grace of vision capable of pacifying that aforementioned multitude of obstacles—the wise, having directly perceived you, the Swan, who are ever-arisen and whose nature is light, with an exceedingly pure vision, cast off the blinding darkness of delusion.

They declare that ignorance—which consists of the hope for permanence in the impermanent, the obsession with purity in the impure, the attachment to a self in what is not-self, and the notion of happiness in great suffering; which is fourfold, difficult to pierce, incessant, and fully developed—is the root of the tree of existence, having destroyed all innate light.

The wise declare that ignorance (*avidyā*)—which is perpetually transformed in four ways, consisting of the hope for permanence in the impermanent, the obsession with purity in the impure, the notion of a self in the non-self, and the perception of pleasure in great suffering—is the root of the tree of worldly existence; it is difficult to pierce and its own nature is utterly destroyed. Men whose vision is inevitably defiled by this [ignorance] perform the movement of a ball within existence due to the destruction of discernment (*viveka*). Having obtained [this state] through various forms of worship...
Those of pure intellect, through the perfection of their meditative absorption which shatters the fear of worldly existence, do not encounter the calamity of rebirth again.

By this [ignorance], the vision of men is corrupted regarding the light of reality; with their discernment destroyed, they repeatedly perform the movement of a ball within cyclic existence through their various practices. However, having attained the meditative absorption (*samādhi*) that shatters the fear of existence, those of pure intellect do not, by virtue of its perfection, suffer the calamity of rebirth. Neither did the sun shine in the sky with its dense masses of rays, nor did the moon dispel the darkness with its beams, for [the world was obscured].
Furthermore, O Lord, no other light—whether from stars, planets, fire, gems, medicinal herbs, lightning, lamps, or the like—was ever seen anywhere before.

The universe had become shrouded in darkness, a certain profound and impenetrable abode; then, having manifested the weight of His own great majesty through the power of His will, the Lord divided Himself by His own free portions—earth, water, wind, fire, moon, and sun—and created the three worlds. Who else but You could do this? (A yugma). *Anvaya*: O Lord! Formerly (before creation), the sun did not shine in the sky with its dense masses of rays of intense luster.
Even the moon did not dispel the darkness with its rays; nor was any other light—the stars, planets, fire, gems, medicinal herbs, lightning, or lamps—seen anywhere.

O Lord! That entire universe became shrouded in darkness, becoming an impenetrable and profound abode (like an exceedingly deep house). Then, [the Lord] manifested Himself as the Great Splendor, made manifest by His own power of will (*svecchā-śakti*).
Who else but You, having divided [the primal matter] into portions consisting of earth, water, air, fire, moon, sun, and ether, could have created the three worlds? (The meaning is: no one at all.
In this beginningless cycle of existence (*saṃsāra*), individual souls (*aṇu*)—their intellects obscured by passion (*rajas*)—perform actions that are auspicious, terrible, or mixed.
Thereafter, Your heart filled with fresh compassion, You bring about all their creation of bodies and worlds for the sake of experiencing those [fruits of action]. (10)
This entire triple world manifested by Your mere volition belongs to You, the Lord who are worshiped by the universe;
for here, O Master, in the case of all objects, Your two innate powers—action and knowledge—are eternally operative in You alone, independent of any instruments.

(11) (A yugma) Anvaya: O Blessed One! In this beginningless saṃsāra, the individual souls (*aṇu*s), whose intellects are afflicted by *rajas*, [perceive] that which is auspicious, or terrible, or variegated.

Or, as they perform their duties, for the sake of their enjoyment of that [world]—[meaning, for the sake of experiencing that threefold karma consisting of a mixture of the auspicious and the inauspicious]—you, whose heart is filled with fresh compassion, ordain the entire creation of the world; this, O Lord, is merely the sport (*līlā*) of you, the Master who makes manifest the entire triple world by his mere resolve and who is honored by the worlds. Why so? O Master!

In this world, that which belongs to you alone— your innate, eternal, and instrument-independent capacity for action and knowledge (the powers of action and knowledge)— which prevails over all objects (serving as the support of all),
follows this well-known path: there can be no diverse creation without a creator, and he cannot be devoid of knowledge.
Therefore, in this wondrous triple world, the Creator must necessarily be a knower; and you are that one. As for others, what can those of ruined intellect possibly dispute against you? (12)

O Lord! This path is well-established—that a diverse creation cannot come into being without a creator, and that such a creator cannot be devoid of knowledge (meaning this is known even to children). Therefore, in this diverse triple world, it is necessarily appropriate that the creator be a knower (omniscient);
and you alone are that omniscient Supreme Self. Why do others of impaired intellect dispute with You?

Now, if they should say this: "Does this God exert himself independently in the creation of the three worlds with a mind not impelled by another? In the first case, he would have no sovereignty, for one who is subject to another lacks power; or in the second case, aiming at what fruit does he strive? (13)

The logical connection (*anvaya*) is as follows: Now, if those common folk were to speak thus—"Does this God exert himself in the creation of the three worlds with a mind impelled by another, or does he exert himself independently?"—in the first case, for one who is subject to another's will (impelled by another), there is indeed no sovereignty;
or in the second case, does he exert himself with some specific fruit in view?

Now, this desire arises [in him]: "For men, there is no liberation without the exhaustion of karma; yet even that [exhaustion] is not possible anywhere without experience (bhoga). Experience does not occur without a substratum, nor is there a body without a world. Therefore, the creation of bodies and worlds is necessary for living beings. (14)
The logical connection (*anvaya*) is as follows: Now, this desire arises in him [the Lord]: "Liberation for human beings is not possible without the destruction of karma;
yet that destruction of karma is nowhere appropriate without experience (*bhoga*). Experience, too, does not occur without a substratum, and that substratum is the body;
furthermore, even the body does not exist without the world. Therefore, the creation of the bodies and the worlds of living beings is fitting."

This is logical: why does a compassionate one, who is impelled by an intense compassion that is sweet as thick nectar and who is constantly devoted to the task of securing the welfare of others, not create the entire world as happy? Or else, why was this person born here afflicted by mental anguish and physical disease? (15)

Is this appropriate for the Lord, who is impelled by an inner compassion as sweet as the dense nectar of its continuity, and who is constantly devoted to the task of accomplishing the welfare of others?
If he is indeed compassionate, why does that Master not create the entire world as happy? Why, in this world, has he produced people afflicted by mental anguish and physical disease?

Now, as for that which constitutes the material cause (*upādāna*) of the world—be it atoms and so forth—as well as the auxiliary causes such as karma and time: if this Lord is not capable of creation without these two, then what is the use of Him? Let that [material cause] alone be manifest as the one skilled in the construction of bodies and the universe. (16)

Sequence: Now, if this Lord is not capable of creation without both that which serves as the material cause for the creation of the world—such as atoms and so forth—and likewise that which serves as the auxiliary cause—such as karma, necessity, and so on—then what is the use of such a Lord?
Let those two alone be manifest as being skilled in the construction of bodies and the universe!

Thus, O Giver of Boons, these dull-witted ones, whose minds are deluded and whose mouths are made clamorous by the arrogance of fallacious reasoning, do not recognize You—the conscious Supreme Person, the compassionate Sovereign of the multitude of inert things—as their Lord for the sake of further bewildering the intellects of the ignorant here. 17.

The grammatical connection (*anvaya*) is as follows: Thus, O Giver of Boons! O Lord! these dull-witted ones of deluded minds, whose mouths are made clamorous by the proficiency of fallacious reasoning, do not know You—the Supreme Person, the conscious presiding deity of the insentient world—as the Compassionate One (the ocean of mercy), for the purpose of bewildering the intellects of the ignorant in this world.

Just as the clay is the material cause, and following that, O Giver of Boons, this entire collection of inert things—the staff, water, wheel, and thread—cannot succeed in the fashioning of a jar without the effort of the potter; so too, the process of worldly existence does not come to pass without You as its presiding controller. (18)

Logical connection (*anvaya*): O Giver of Boons! Here, clay is the material cause (*upādāna*) of the jar; thereafter, the staff, water, the wheel, and the string—this entire collection of insentient things—is like the potter's effort; just as these are not capable of producing a jar (*kumbhaghaṭana*) without the potter’s exertion, so too the process of existence (*bhavavidhi*) does not occur without You as the presiding controller (*adhiṣṭhātṛ*).

Ignorant of the truth, the fool performs harsh and uneven actions; their ripening falls upon him in the mire of worldly existence and affliction. Therefore, the light of knowledge—which reveals the depths of all objects—is absolutely necessary for one whose vision is obscured by the darkness of great delusion. (19)

One who lacks discernment performs harsh and uneven actions without even understanding them; when the ripening of that action occurs, he falls into the mire of the afflictions of existence. Therefore, for a person whose vision is obscured by the darkness of great delusion, the light of knowledge—which reveals the depths of all objects—is absolutely necessary.
The means for attaining that [liberation] exists, but there is no other way apart from the scripture; and here, the scripture is nothing other than what has been taught by You, the Knower of Reality.
Discerning what is beneficial and what is harmful, the wise perform these [deeds], applying themselves to what is beneficial and abandoning what is harmful; thus, they do not deserve to fall.

O Lord! Since there is no other means for attaining that [liberation] than the scripture (*śāstra*), and since that scripture has not been taught by you, it does not exist [for us]. Therefore, because the virtuous (*santaḥ*) distinguish between what is beneficial and what is harmful, apply themselves to the beneficial, and abandon the harmful, these [virtuous ones] do not deserve to fall.

You have directly realized the Dharma through the splendor of innate wisdom, thereby destroying the darkness of men; thereafter, you established it by means of instruction. Your word is the authority, for it is not fitting for the Blessed One—the Lord of the World, whose mind is overwhelmed by profound compassion—to speak what is false.

Anvaya: O All-pervading Lord! You manifested Dharma directly through the splendor of Your innate knowledge; thereafter, by means of its instruction, You brought about the destruction of the darkness [of ignorance] for men.

Indeed, Your word is authoritative; for it is not proper to declare false the speech of the Blessed One, the Lord of the Universe, whose mind is overwhelmed by intense compassion. Therefore, O Giver of Boons, this world—plunged in a mass of mud of the thickest darkness—should be regarded by You as Your own innate [kin].
O Hara, he who, having bound himself with faith, repeatedly exerts himself to perform that which has been taught by You, crosses the ocean of saṃsāra, so difficult to traverse. || 22 ||

O Hara! O Giver of Boons! This world, submerged in a dense mass of the mire of profound darkness, having contemplated—that is, having respectfully recognized—this innate compassion of Yours (as previously described), has repeatedly set out to practice what You have declared; and maintaining a bond of faith, it crosses the ocean of saṃsāra, though it is difficult to traverse.

Thus, O Blessed One, having created a universe devoid of humans through Your unfailing majesty, and having subsequently expanded it with abundant displays of power, You now desire to withdraw everything back into Your own glory and attain the bliss of liberation (*kaivalya*), which arises from the cessation of the exertion involved in tossing that [universe] about like a ball.
[The grammatical connection: O Blessed One! Thus, being one of unfailing majesty (independent), You—having first [created] the universe which was devoid of humans (consisting of darkness)—...

Having first brought forth the universe through expansive sequences of manifestation, and having expanded it (endowed with life), you then withdraw that entire world into your own glory; thus, O Lord, you desire for yourself the state of absolute liberation (*kaivalya*), filled with the bliss arising from the cessation of the exertion involved in tossing that ball.

What more need be said? O All-pervading One, supreme in compassion for your devotees, may this [state] come to me through the grace of Your pair of lotus feet, which shatters the fear of worldly existence.

May there be devotion to the ritual of worshipping your lotus feet until my body is free from disease; and may there be liberation before you alone for one whose mind is focused on you throughout life. (24)

The syntactical connection (*anvaya*): O All-pervading Lord! O Destroyer of the fear of worldly existence! O Thou most intent on compassion for Thy devotees! What is the use of much speaking in this manner?

By the grace of the pair of Thy lotus feet—that devotion which exists toward the rite of worshipping Thy lotus feet, a body free from disease for as long as life lasts, and then liberation before Thee alone for one whose mind is fixed on Thee—may all this be mine.

"O Lord, O God! I consider it to be like a flower in the sky that another birth will come to me, who have thus obtained grace through the recitation of Your praise. O Protector, if that [birth] were produced by the remnants of past karma, what would be the use of further [effort]? May I, being once again liberated, exist only for the sake of praising Your lotus-feet. *Anvaya:* O God! O Blessed One! Thus, for me—who am fortunate—having obtained grace through the recitation of Your praise, another birth will come to pass; so I think. *Note on terminology:* * *Khapuṣpa*: "sky-flower," a metaphor for something non-existent or impossible. * *Prasāda*: Grace or favor. * *Nirvṛta*: Liberated or at peace. * *Pādakamala*: Lotus-feet (a respectful term for the feet of a deity). * *IAST diacritics*: Used for Sanskrit terms as requested. The output uses standard IAST transliteration.

If I consider [this world] to be like a flower in the sky, produced by the remnants of past karma, then what is the use of further speech? O Lord! Even in that case, may I once again find fulfillment through the praise of your lotus feet.
Thus ends [the hymn] to the Blessed Maheśvara, composed by the great Kashmiri poet Śrī Jagaddharabhaṭṭa, accompanied by the *Premamakaranda*.
In the *Stutikusumāñjali*, the hymn titled "Praise of the Lord" (*Īśvara-praśaṃsā*) is completed. This is the thirty-sixth hymn:

O Lord, all those born [in this world] do not defile themselves, nor do they give cause for suspicion even toward those who delight in acts of malice; rather, the deer-eyed women desire them with longing.
Those who gaze [upon you] mark their foreheads with the dust of your lotus feet. || 1 ||
Anvaya: O Lord! Blessed are those who do not defile their entire lives; who do not even suspect enemies who delight in acts of malice;
whom deer-eyed women gaze upon with longing; and who mark their own foreheads with the dust of Your lotus feet.
They render the desires of their enemies fruitless within their hearts and bestow the nectar of knowledge upon the wretched. Even kings [bow] to their words.
Those who worship you with the supernatural power of flowers consisting of words of praise do not transgress [your command]. || 2 ||

Blessed are those who frustrate the desires of their enemies in their hearts and bestow the nectar of knowledge upon the wretched; even kings do not transgress the words of those who worship you with the profusion of flowers that are their hymns of praise. They bring forth the abundant fruit of their birth and liberate both themselves and others from the calamities of suffering; even their innate enemies cannot [overcome] them.
Those who deceive you, the protector and kinsman of the helpless, yet pay you honor. || 3 ||

O Lord! Those who worship You, the kinsman of the helpless, bring forth the abundant fruit of Your birth; they liberate themselves and others from the calamities of affliction; even those innate enemies do not deceive them;
they acquire the Dharma, beautiful as the rays of the moon; they delight even the hearts of the wise with their words; and even the frowns of Death do not threaten them.
Those who worship you, O Hara, the remover of the disease of worldly existence— || 4 ||

O Hara! Those who worship you, the remover of the disease of worldly existence, acquire merit as beautiful as the rays of the moon; they delight even the hearts of the wise with their words, and even the frowns of Death do not threaten them.

They bolt the door of their hearts against your praise—that is, they keep it ever-present—and they utterly shatter the tree of suffering even in times of calamity. Such is your very nature upon this earth.
Those who, like children, cause the dancer of speech to dance before you. || 5 ||
O All-pervading Lord! Those who, in the chamber of their hearts, bolt shut the door against Your praise; those who, in times of calamity, firmly cleave asunder the tree of suffering;
those who, like children, wander upon this earth in the very essence of Your being (the flavor of meditation); those who dance the drama of their own speech before You;

those who utterly shatter the shackles of the ropes of karma with their well-spoken words; and those who adorn the ears of the wise with their eloquent verses—even they [are unable to cross] the ocean of worldly existence, despite their devotion to You.
But those who ferry across your mind serve as caskets for the wealth of their hymns of praise.

For those who, with well-spoken verses, utterly shatter the fetters of the rope of karma; who adorn the ears of the wise; who provide a boat for crossing even the ocean of worldly existence; who act as a casket for the wealth of hymns offered to Your mind;

who grind away their sins like fragments of stone; who, by their speech, cause even the flowers of the gods to tremble; and who likewise [tremble] before You in this world—[they alone attain liberation].
Those who bring to their ears the glories of the wise and describe your praises; || 7 ||

They crush their own sins like fragments of stone with their words; they cause even the brows of the virtuous to quiver; and in this world, they make their own fame heard by describing tales of praise for you before the wise.
They do not have even the Māras slain in battle out of compassion, nor do they inflict torment even upon those who have provoked their anger; they dispel the sorrow of the world with fearlessness.
Those who cast their crest-jewels at your feet. || 8 ||

Those who cast themselves at the crest of your feet find that, even when engaged in battle, they do not cause the Māras to be slain out of compassion; even when provoked to anger, they do not torment the world with grief, but rather dispel it through fearlessness.
With their well-spoken words, they cut asunder the heavy fetters of sin within their hearts and turn back the longing for enjoyments in the sense-objects.
They cause even the minds of sentient beings to dance who proclaim your deeds, O Moon-crested One. || 9 ||

O Moon-crested Lord! Those who proclaim your life-story sever the great noose of sin within their hearts, turn away from the longing for enjoyment in sense-objects, and even cause the minds of the conscious to dance through their well-spoken verses;
they destroy the misdeeds of this birth, cause those of pure intellect to recite these beautiful hymns, and indeed make even the lute-players and actors sing them aloud.
Out of devotion, they offer hymns of praise to you. || 10 ||

Those who devoutly offer hymns of praise to you cause the misdeeds of their births to perish, cause well-spoken verses to resound through those of stainless intellect, and cause even lute-players and actors to sing their songs. They urge even their enemies toward virtuous deeds and delight the hearts of the wise with their words; yet, not even a trace of sorrow remains in their minds.
Those who do not disparage your deeds, but rather rejoice in them. || 11 ||

They overcome even their enemies by urging them toward virtuous deeds with their words, and they delight the hearts of the good; in the minds of those who rejoice in your exploits, no sorrows ever arise.

They do not distress even those whose minds are fierce in conflict, but shatter the delusion that resembles a firm bolt within the heart. They display their own skill even to those of gentle intellect.
Those who proclaim your own hymns offer them as a presentation.

Those who offer their own well-spoken verses before You cause even those of fierce and harsh minds no distress; they shatter the delusion that is like a firm bolt in the heart. They reveal their own skill even to those of dull intellect. For those who have taken refuge in You, the creepers of speech cause devotion to swell and strike the root of attachment in the heart—even for those who have turned toward other philosophical systems. You [do this] even for them.
Those who offer praise with a flood of words gladden your heart.

Those people who, through the creeper of their speech, delight Your heart—those who, by their own cleverness, cause even those proponents who have entered other systems (even those on crooked paths) to bow to You (to honor You), and who intensify devotion in the hearts of those who have sought refuge (in order to hear the means for crossing the ocean of worldly existence)—they indeed cross over that very ocean.

They cause the creeper of speech to blossom within the hearts of those devoted to You, and they provoke longing even in those who follow other views. It is they who, by the flood of Your words, bring joy to Your heart.

Those wise ones who worship you with ever-new and fresh offerings, and who drink [the nectar] as sweet as the essence of sugarcane, increase their success in the fruits of worldly enjoyment and liberation; they accomplish virtuous deeds, attain bliss, and pacify all mental anguish. (14)

Those wise ones who nourish with fresh and ever-new hymns you— who grant the successful attainment of both worldly enjoyment and liberation, increase virtuous deeds, and accomplish peace that calms all mental anguish—
they do not provoke even the most formidable enemies in battle, and they purify their hearts with the nectar of knowledge, even toward the enmity arising in the hearts of their foes.
Those who restrain you with their own words of praise awaken you. 15.
In battle, even those who are fierce do not fight with them; they purify the heart with the nectar of knowledge; they restrain within the hearts of even their enemies the fire born of wrath;
and they awaken you with their own words of praise.
They humble the arrogant in the assembly of the wise and honor the mature with humility. Prosperities attend them.
Those who themselves pass their days in a manner unequaled by others, conducting them with ever-new tranquility.

Those who, being self-controlled, treat the arrogant with contempt in the assembly of the wise, yet honor the mature by bowing with humility— those peerless ones toward whom prosperity comes of its own accord, those fortunate ones who spend their days in your [service];
they travel the path of the humble without fear, they cause even enemies who do not tremble to suffer, and they cause even those like cattle to abandon affliction and calamity.
Having propitiated you, O Lord, they cause their vision to be granted. || 17 ||

O Lord! Those who, having propitiated You, cause You to cast Your glance upon them, lead the humble (those who bow before them) along a path free from fear; they do not torment even trembling enemies; they cause even those equal to cattle to escape the calamity of suffering;
they subdue the fierce pride of the intoxicated and drive away greed from the abode of the virtuous; and they satisfy the multitudes of supplicants with gifts and other means.
They place their crowns at the soles of Your feet. || 18 ||

Those who place their crowns at your feet, O Lord, cause the fierce and intoxicated Antaka (Death) to be subdued; they drive away greed from the abodes of the virtuous and satisfy the multitudes of supplicants with gifts and other means. In the houses of the good, they diminish great calamities and offer themselves as a bed for you who desire to rest; they also perform acts of service for those touched by distress.
Those fools who conceptualize [you] even as something new speak of you in such a manner. || 19 ||
Those who, out of compassion, provide a bed for you when you wish to lie down—that is, when you desire to rest—in the houses of the virtuous;
who perform services for those touched by affliction; who cause even children to speak of you as new [in their praise];

who do not become angry even with those whose minds are guilty; who conceal the vast heat of suffering through their own humility; and who place your stainless glory upon their own intellects—they truly honor you.
They never neglect your worship at any time. || 20 ||
Those who never fail in your worship—though their minds may be guilty of transgression, they do not provoke anger; though they suffer great distress in adversity, they conceal it with shame;
and they establish those of pure intellect in your abode—they, O Lord, manifest unimpeded power upon the earth and cause supreme joy to those of disciplined mind, even unto the three lineages.
Those who adorn you with their own [verses] and entice you with their own eloquent hymns of praise. || 21 ||
Those who manifest unimpeded power upon the earth, inspire supreme joy in the wise, and bring glory to their own three lineages; those who entice you with their own eloquent hymns of praise;
they rescue the afflicted people submerged in calamity, discerning the true from the false through their intellect, and ward off ignorance and pride in those possessed of it.
O Moon-bearer, those who maintain devotion to you within their hearts.
They rescue distressed people submerged in calamity; having reflected with their intellect, they discern between the good and the bad; and they dispel the ignorance of those who bow before them.

O Bearer of the Moon! Those persons who hold devotion to you in their hearts win over even their enemies, however steadfast in their wrath, and they uproot delusion as one would a tree. And [they place] your command upon their heads.
Those who bow their foreheads to the great ones and dust them with the pollen of your feet. || 23 ||

Those who dust their foreheads with the pollen of your feet—even if they are enemies of long-standing resentment—win over even the most stubborn foes; they uproot delusion like a tree and place the commands of the great upon their heads.
They wash away the mud clinging to their own bodies and purify the entire circle of the quarters, reducing all afflictions in an instant like a heap of grass.
Those who cause you to be offered as a sacrifice and contemplate you within their hearts as one whose body is radiant light.

Those who meditate upon you, whose body is light, within their hearts, wash away the mud clinging to their souls and purify the entire horizon; they instantly mow down the clusters of afflictions like blades of grass.
They diminish the heavy calamities in their homes, refine their own skill, and bring joy to the hearts of the virtuous.
Those who inscribe hymns of praise to you in the temples of the gods reveal [the truth]. || 25 ||

Those who display hymns of praise to you in the abodes of the wise nourish stainless merit within themselves and dry up the impurity of the mire of evil deeds in their hearts; they alleviate the heavy calamities that have befallen them and manifest their own skill, while reflecting favorably upon the minds of the virtuous and instilling joy in their hearts. Even those who are cruel and distressed by enmity [are moved by them].
Those who indeed please him cry out, "Śiva, Śiva! || 26 ||

They augment stainless merit within themselves and thoroughly dry up the mire of evil karma in their hearts; they satisfy even cruel men who are embroiled in hostility by chanting the name "Śiva, Śiva.
They adorn the entire world with their deeds and do not offend those who are angry or hostile in heart, nor even the most formidable enemy-soldiers.
Those who provoke your mind, O Śiva, with passion, they instead bring it satisfaction.

O Śiva! Those people who, through their own deeds, adorn the entire universe; who do not offend those with hostile hearts nor provoke the enraged; and who do not incense even the most formidable soldiers of Yama—those who, out of passion [meaning either the flavor of devotion to you or the singing of passionate hymns, as it is said: "Śaṅkara is pleased by song and instrumental music"] delight your mind.

They rain upon you in their hearts that thirst for the water of compassion; they draw out even the serpents of sin dwelling within their minds. Making Yama tremble, they defy him with their eyebrows, and they gladden you, O Hara, with their own words of praise—even with new ones. (28)

O Hara! Those who gladden you with their own words of praise cause rain to fall upon their hearts that are parched by the thirst for the water of compassion; they draw out even the serpents of sin from within; and by merely raising a tremor in their eyebrows—meaning, by a mere sign of the brow—they subdue Yama. Though their speech may be sealed in silence, they provoke laughter with their words and perfume the faces of the wise. They [gladden] the universe.
They illuminate the mind with stainless glories and cause it to blossom anew. || 29 ||

They, whose speech is sealed by silence, yet cause the faces of the wise to smile with their words; who perfume the world with their stainless fame and illuminate it with their splendor; who cause your mind to blossom with their new [compositions];
they paint even the walls of the hearts of the wicked and turn even hostile men, arrogant in their anger, into friends; and with the nectar of their well-spoken verses, they purify the very earth.
Those whose speech is a boat cross over your ocean of conduct by means of it. || 30 ||

Blessed are those who, by means of the boat of their speech, navigate across the ocean of your life-story; they paint the mental walls of even the wicked, they turn hostile people—even those arrogant with rage—into friends with the nectar of their well-spoken words, and they purify the very earth itself.
They nourish the hearts of the virtuous and utterly destroy external and internal enemies; yet they do not reproach themselves, even when their own foes are bowed down before them.
But those who honor you with fresh hymns of praise and offerings of wealth... || 31 ||

Those who honor you with new hymns of praise cause the hearts of the virtuous to swell with joy and utterly destroy both external and internal enemies; though their own selves are already bowed in humility, they do not reproach themselves.
They lift up their souls which were submerged in the turbid mire of impurity and wash away the stains, dark as a swarm of bees, with the waters of wisdom. And having remembered you—
Those who, out of the impetuosity of negligence, strike their shoulders, yet by devotion to you cause their entire mind to be cleansed of all impurity.
Those who, by remembering you, uplift their own souls submerged in the turbidity of impurity; who wash away the darkness as black as a swarm of bees with the waters of knowledge;

who, out of the impulse of joy, strike their shoulders upon remembering you; and who, through devotion to you, stir up their entirely lethargic minds—they awaken the dormant passion in the hearts of beautiful women and open the hearts of the virtuous in the assembly to offer them praise.
O Giver of Boons, those who are arrogant and crooked-minded do not pierce your heart anywhere, for they merely moisten it with their piteous cries of distress.

O Giver of Boons! Those who awaken the dormant passion in the hearts of beautiful women, who open the minds of the virtuous to receive praise in the assembly, and who—being arrogant, cruel, crooked-minded, and deceitful—never find any flaw in them;
those fortunate ones who moisten your heart with their piteous cries of lamentation.
They cause tears to flow from the eyes of the members of the assembly; they drive far away the heavy burden of the great anger of men;
with their well-spoken verses, they melt the hearts of the virtuous like moonlight melts a gem; O Master, they make you hear these ever-new utterances. 34.
